question.explanation:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

  • If $|6x+1| = 6x+1,$ we obtain: \begin{align} |6x+1| &= 7 \\[5pt] 6x+1 &= 7 \\[5pt] 6x &= 6 \\[5pt] \dfrac{6x}{6} &= \dfrac66 \\[5pt] x &= 1 \end{align}

  • If $|6x+1| = -(6x+1),$ we obtain: \begin{align} |6x+1| &= 7 \\[5pt] -(6x+1) &= 7 \\[5pt] -6x - 1 &= 7 \\[5pt] -6x &= 8 \\[5pt] \dfrac{-6x}{-6} &= \dfrac{8}{-6} \\[5pt] x &= -\dfrac43 \end{align}

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-\dfrac{4}{3}$ and $x=1.$

question.text: Which of the following is equivalent to $(q + 1)(q^2 + 7q + 2)?$
question.explanation:
We distribute both terms of the binomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify:

\begin{align*} (q + 1)(q^2 + 7q + 2) &=\\[3pt] q(q^2 + 7q + 2) + 1(q^2 + 7q + 2)&=\\[3pt] q^3 + 7q^2 + 2q + q^2 + 7q + 2&=\\[3pt] q^3 + 8q^2 + 9q + 2 \end{align*}

Before we start our normal process of factoring, notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $ \dfrac{1}{4}.$ Therefore, we can simplify the expression by factoring out $ \dfrac{1}{4},$ as follows: \[ \dfrac{s^2}{4}-\dfrac{1}{36} = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(s^2-\dfrac{1}{9}\right) \]

Now, let's factor the expression inside parentheses using the difference of squares formula:

\begin{align*} s^2-\dfrac{1}{9} &=\\[5pt] s^2-\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 &=\\[5pt] \left(s - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(s + \dfrac{1}{3}\right) \end{align*}

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows: \[ \dfrac{s^2}{4}-\dfrac{1}{36} = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(s - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(s + \dfrac{1}{3}\right) \]

example.title: Using the Power of Product Rule with a Positive Power

question.text: Museum attendance increased to $120\%$ of last year’s total. Of those visitors, $90\%$ also attended the art exhibit. What percentage of last year’s total attended the art exhibit?
question.explanation:
Let $x$ be the number of visitors last year.

We're told that attendance increased to $120\%$ of last year’s total. Thus, the new number of visitors is $1.2x.$

We are also told that of those visitors, $90\%$ attended the art exhibit. So, the number of visitors who attended the art exhibit is \[ 0.9(1.2x) = 1.08x. \]

The expression $1.08x$ represents $108\%$ of $x.$ Therefore, $108\%$ of last year’s total attended the art exhibit.

question.text:
Which of the following values of $x$ satisfy the inequality $\dfrac{x}{5} \gt 2\,?$

  1. $x=30$
  2. $x=15$
  3. $x=10$
question.explanation:
We substitute each value into the given inequality and check to see if the resulting statement is true or false.

  • We substitute the value ${\color{blue}x}={\color{blue}30}$ into the given inequality. We get: \begin{align} \dfrac{\color{blue}x}{5} & \gt 2 \\ \dfrac{\color{blue}30}{5} & \gt 2 \\ 6 & \gt 2\quad \color{green}\large{\checkmark} \end{align} So, substituting $x=30$ into the inequality leads to a true statement.

    Therefore, $x=30$ satisfies this inequality.

  • We substitute the value ${\color{blue}x}={\color{blue}15}$ into the given inequality. We get: \begin{align} \dfrac{\color{blue}x}{5} & \gt 2 \\ \dfrac{\color{blue}15}{5} & \gt 2 \\ 3 & \gt 2 \quad \color{green}\large{\checkmark} \end{align} So, substituting $x=15$ into the inequality leads to a true statement.

    Therefore, $x=15$ satisfies this inequality.

  • We substitute the value ${\color{blue}x}={\color{blue}10}$ into the given inequality. We get: \begin{align} \dfrac{\color{blue}x}{5} & \gt 2 \\ \dfrac{\color{blue}10}{5} & \gt 2 \\ 2 & \gt 2 \quad \color{red}\large{\times} \end{align} So, substituting $x=10$ into the inequality leads to a false statement.

    Therefore, $x=10$ does not satisfy this inequality.
